title: Undo relies on a shallow-clone snapshot whose Maps/entities are shared-mutable — load-bearing but undocumented
evidence: store.ts:202 `snapshot: st.snapshot ? { ...st.snapshot } : st.snapshot` — bumpSnapshot does a top-level-only spread; the campaignById/adSetById/adById Map instances (Snapshot extends Dataset, types.ts:18) are copied by reference, so clones share the same Maps and entity objects. captureRestore resolves entities through those Maps (store.ts:212-215) and the restore closure re-resolves + mutates them in place (store.ts:221-226). demoProvider.applyAction mutates the very same entities in place (demoProvider.ts:28,32 and applyStatus 60-70). So apply and Undo both write the same shared object — which is exactly why Undo works after a version bump. The mechanism the candidate describes is accurate.
note: Mechanically correct, but this is an observation about an undocumented load-bearing invariant, not a live bug — nothing in the current codebase diffs before/after by object identity, so there is no defect today. Severity low is right (arguably nit). One reinforcing detail the candidate missed: bumpSnapshot's own existing comment (store.ts:197-198) literally says "clone the snapshot reference," which is the kind of phrasing that could mislead a future reader into assuming deep/independent copies — so the suggested clarifying comment is well-placed. Note the restore closure correctly captures primitives (prevStatus/prevBudget, store.ts:219-220) rather than relying on object identity, so Undo itself is robust against the shared-state pitfall; the residual risk is purely for hypothetical future code (e.g. before/after diffing or concurrent re-loads via init()) that would wrongly trust {...snapshot} as immutable. Doc-only fix; no functional change needed.
suggestedFix: Add a comment at bumpSnapshot clarifying the clone is intentionally shallow (entities stay shared so in-place provider writes + Undo both work). If any future feature needs an immutable before/after, capture primitive field values (as captureRestore already does) rather than relying on object identity.

title: Native date inputs hardcode [color-scheme:dark] but the app supports a real, user-reachable light theme
evidence: DateRangeMenu.tsx:74 and :83 both set className "input px-2 py-1 text-xs [color-scheme:dark]" on the two <input type="date"> elements. index.css:33 sets color-scheme:dark on :root and index.css:57 sets color-scheme:light on [data-theme='light']. store.ts:113-118 toggleTheme() applies document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', theme) and persists it; Sidebar.tsx:28,97 wires toggleTheme to a clickable control, so light mode is genuinely reachable. The .input base class (index.css:135-136) does NOT declare color-scheme, so the inline [color-scheme:dark] is the sole, overriding source on these inputs — in light mode the native UA date-picker controls render dark against a light surface.
note: Claim is accurate and not handled elsewhere — .input doesn't set color-scheme, so nothing counteracts the hardcoded dark in light mode. The suggested fix of simply deleting [color-scheme:dark] is the cleaner of the two options: the inputs then inherit color-scheme from the [data-theme] root cascade automatically, making the store-theme-conditional alternative unnecessary. Genuinely cosmetic and minor (affects only the native calendar popup/spinner chrome of the custom-range inputs, only in light mode, only when the custom-range section is expanded), so low severity stands. Note dark is the default theme, so most users never hit this.
suggestedFix: Drop the hardcoded [color-scheme:dark] and let it inherit from the [data-theme] root (index.css already sets color-scheme per theme), or make it conditional on the store theme.

title: setTimeout-based toast auto-dismiss is never cancelled and can fire removeToast on a stale id after manual dismiss
evidence: store.ts:175 `setTimeout(() => get().removeToast(id), action ? 7000 : 4200)` discards the timer handle. store.ts:178-179 removeToast is `toasts.filter((t) => t.id !== id)` — a no-op once the id is gone. Toasts.tsx:33-35 (Undo path) and Toasts.tsx:41 (dismiss button) both call `remove(t.id)` immediately, after which the original timer still fires harmlessly. store.ts:65 `genId = () => Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)` yields fresh ids per toast, so a stale timer cannot hit a different live toast — confirming the 'harmless' framing.
note: Every claim in the rationale checks out against the code, including the self-described 'harmless' impact. Caveats that keep this firmly a nit, not higher: (1) timers are bounded — each self-clears within 4.2–7s, so there is no unbounded leak; even with rapid actions the pending-timer count is bounded by toast creation rate over a ~7s window. (2) Toasts is a persistent shell component (rendered once, never conditionally unmounted in normal use), so the 'no way to cancel on unmount' concern is essentially theoretical here. (3) No user-visible bug and no correctness risk because ids are unique random strings, so a late timer can never evict the wrong toast. The suggested fix is sound; the cleanest version is the second option — move auto-dismiss into the Toasts component via a per-toast useEffect with a clearTimeout cleanup, which ties the timer to lifecycle and naturally cancels on manual dismiss/Undo (the toast unmounts when removed from state). Storing a Map<id, handle> in the store and clearing it in removeToast also works but pushes imperative timer bookkeeping into the store. Either way this is a low-priority hygiene item.
suggestedFix: Store timeout handles keyed by toast id and clearTimeout in removeToast; or move auto-dismiss into the Toasts component with a per-toast useEffect cleanup so timers are tied to component lifecycle.

title: useSnapshot's bare useStore((s)=>s.version) subscription is redundant, not the rendering linchpin
evidence: src/app/hooks.ts:6-9 — `useSnapshot` selects `s.snapshot` (line 7) then calls `useStore((s) => s.version)` (line 8) purely for its subscription side effect, returning only `snapshot`. So the literal observation is correct. BUT the rationale is refuted by src/app/store.ts:197-204: `bumpSnapshot` always sets BOTH `version: st.version + 1` AND `snapshot: { ...st.snapshot }` in the same `set` call. Every version bump therefore also produces a fresh snapshot object reference, which zustand's default `Object.is` equality on the line-7 `s.snapshot` selector already detects → re-render fires from line 7 alone. `version` is read nowhere else in the codebase (grep: only hooks.ts:8 reads it; store.ts only writes it). `applySuggestion` early-returns if `!snapshot` (store.ts ~118) and setThreshold/resetThresholds run post-load, so no version-bump path skips the snapshot clone.
note: Two parts of the candidate split: the factual description (bare side-effect subscription) is true; the risk model is wrong. Line 8 is NOT the linchpin — it's redundant belt-and-suspenders given bumpSnapshot's snapshot clone. Deleting it would NOT silently break optimistic-update rendering today. The "linters often flag" point is also overstated: there is no ESLint config in the repo, tsconfig has noUnusedLocals:false, and a call-expression statement isn't flagged by noUnusedLocals or @typescript-eslint/no-unused-expressions anyway. Sharper framing: this is dead/redundant code, not a fragile dependency. Cleaner fix than the candidate's: just delete line 8 and rely on the snapshot reference clone (the real driver), OR if you want version to be the source of truth, drop the snapshot clone from bumpSnapshot and keep line 8 as `const version = useStore(s=>s.version); void version` with a comment. Keeping both (current state) is harmless but the comment on hooks.ts:5 misleadingly implies version is what drives the re-render. Severity stays nit.
suggestedFix: Make the dependency explicit, e.g. `const version = useStore((s) => s.version); void version` with a comment, or select both in one subscription: `useStore((s) => [s.snapshot, s.version] as const)` with a shallow comparator, so the intent is legible and lint-safe.

title: ScopeSwitcher recomputes metricsForScope per client on every render while open
evidence: ScopeSwitcher.tsx:80-81 calls metricsForScope(snapshot, {kind:'client', clientId:c.id}, range) inside clients.map with no memo. metricsForScope at src/lib/selectors.ts:63-65 -> metricsForAdIds (selectors.ts:55-57) -> adIdsForScope (client branch -> adIdsForClient, Map lookup) + insightsForAdIds (walks each ad's rows, selectors.ts:46-53) + filterByRange (metrics.ts:64-66) + aggregate (metrics.ts:19-46). Component subscribes to scope (line 17) and range (line 19), so those store changes re-render and recompute. The whole block is gated behind {open && ...} (line 48), so nothing runs when closed.
note: The mechanism is real but the impact is overstated. (1) Path nit: rationale says selectors.ts:55-65 with no dir; the real file is src/lib/selectors.ts, imported via ../../lib/selectors. (2) Scale: the actual dataset has 7 clients (src/lib/demo/catalog.ts), ~12-18 ads each, 90 days (WINDOW_DAYS) -> roughly ~9.5k numeric adds per full render, i.e. sub-millisecond. "Non-trivial" / "large agency portfolio" is hypothetical, not current. (3) The "recomputes even on unrelated re-renders" justification is weak: the only store slices it subscribes to are scope and range, which are exactly the inputs to the CPA computation — so a recompute on those changes is warranted, not wasted. The only truly wasted recompute is on the open/close useState toggle and parent re-renders. Severity is nit, not low. The suggested fix (useMemo keyed on [snapshot, range] precomputing a clientId->metrics map) is correct and cheap if applied, but this is a defensive/future-proofing cleanup, not a measurable problem today.
suggestedFix: Wrap the per-client CPA computation in a useMemo keyed on [snapshot, range], or precompute a clientId→metrics map once and look it up in the render.

title: Action toast auto-dismisses after 7s with no timer pause on hover/focus (WCAG 2.2.1)
evidence: Toasts.tsx:16-18 container is role="status" aria-live="polite". Toasts.tsx:41 dismiss button has aria-label="Dismiss notification". The Undo action button (Toasts.tsx:31-40) has no aria-label — its accessible name is the visible label text "Undo" (line 38). store.ts:175 sets the auto-dismiss timer: `setTimeout(() => get().removeToast(id), action ? 7000 : 4200)` — action toasts vanish after exactly 7s with no pause-on-hover/focus and no way to re-trigger. The Undo closure (store.ts:145-158) is created per apply-call via captureRestore (store.ts:134) and is attached only to the live toast.
note: Core mechanic is confirmed: an action toast carrying Undo is purely time-boxed at 7s with no timer pause on hover/focus (a real WCAG 2.2.1 "Timing Adjustable" concern for time-limited interactive content). Two sub-claims are overstated: (1) the Undo button IS labeled — "Undo" is a valid accessible name, it's just not uniquely descriptive (e.g. "Undo apply change"), so "no aria-label distinguishing it" is misleading. (2) The suggested "make Undo available from applied[] history" fix is not as cheap as implied: applied[] (store.ts:140-143) records title/message/ts/suggestionId but NOT the restore() closure, so wiring Undo into history requires persisting the restore function too. Sharper, lower-effort fix: pause/clear the setTimeout while the toast is hovered or focus-within, then resume on blur — this is the canonical WCAG 2.2.1 remedy and stays local to pushToast/Toasts. Severity is correctly a nit: demo-mode internal tool, mouse-dismissable, and the change is non-destructive (snapshot revert).
suggestedFix: For toasts carrying an action, either pause the auto-dismiss timer on hover/focus, lengthen it, or make Undo also available from the applied-actions history (store.ts:applied[]) so it isn't purely time-boxed.

title: Aggregated frequency is an impressions-weighted daily average, not cumulative window frequency
evidence: The core mechanism is exactly as claimed and verified end-to-end. metrics.ts:41 `b.frequency = safeDiv(b.impressions, b.reach)`; metrics.ts:24 `b.reach += r.reach` (additive). generate.ts:497-498 generates a per-day frequency then derives `reach = round(impressions/frequency)`, so summing reach makes the roll-up algebraically an impressions-weighted average of DAILY frequency, not cumulative window frequency. types.ts:180 comment confirms reach is an "additive approximation for demo aggregation" without addressing the frequency consequence. It is surfaced verbatim at ClientDashboard.tsx:93 over the default 28d range (app/store.ts:80 `range: makeRange('28d')`), and feeds the fatigue trigger at ai/engine.ts:133 and ai/creative.ts:67 vs `fatigueFrequency: 3.0` (ai/thresholds.ts:31). NOTE: the candidate's file paths are wrong — engine.ts and creative.ts live under src/lib/ai/, not src/lib/.
note: The mechanism is real, but the rationale's central claim — that the fatigue heuristic "can almost never cross its own threshold" — is refuted by the generator. The fatigue archetype is explicitly tuned (generate.ts:435-436: freq0=1.7, freqSlope=3.0) so recent-day daily frequency = clamp(1.7 + 3.0*t - 1, 1.02, 6.5) reaches ~3.4-3.7 at t→1, which clears the 3.0 threshold; healthy ads (freqSlope 0.5-1.4) correctly stay below it. The threshold slider bounds (thresholds.ts:64: 2.5-4.5) match the ~2-3.7 range the formula actually produces, so the engine IS calibrated to this quantity and fires as designed in demo mode. The genuine, narrower defect is semantic/labeling: a 28-day KPI labeled "frequency" in the client strip is an avg-daily-frequency (~2-3), not the cumulative impressions/unique-reach a Meta buyer reads over that window (which would be materially higher as reach saturates). So this is a demo-fidelity / label-accuracy issue, internally self-consistent, not a correctness bug that breaks the engine — hence partial and severity low (not medium). Best fix: rename the surfaced metric to "Avg daily frequency" (or compute a saturating cumulative reach per ad over the window) so the UI label matches the quantity; the engine threshold needs no change.
lane: Data layer & domain model (src/lib types, demo generator, RNG, metrics, selectors, formatting/labels/palette, debug surface)
suggestedFix: Either (a) model a saturating cumulative reach per ad over the window and compute window frequency from impressions / max(cumulative reach), or (b) compute roll-up frequency as a spend/impression-weighted average of per-ad-day frequency explicitly and rename the surfaced metric to 'avg daily frequency' so the engine thresholds and UI label match the actual quantity. At minimum, calibrate fatigueFrequency to the values this formula actually produces.

title: Two duplicate addDays implementations can drift apart
evidence: src/lib/demo/generate.ts:32-36 defines a local (non-exported) addDays; src/lib/metrics.ts:107-111 defines an exported addDays. Both are byte-for-byte identical: `new Date(iso + 'T00:00:00Z')`, `d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() + days)`, `return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10)`. Both copies are actively used in their own concern: generate.ts builds dataset dates (windowDates line 41; createdAt at 141, 327, 381) while metrics.ts builds query windows (enumerateDates 123, makeRange presets 139-153, prev-range 163-164, earliestDate 168). grep confirms exactly these two definitions and no other copy.
note: Claim is accurate, but severity is correctly low: both copies are pure, deterministic, UTC-anchored, and trivial — drift only happens if someone edits one without the other, and the dataset/query split makes such a divergence a real (if unlikely) range-filter bug. The bigger catch is that the SUGGESTED FIX is backwards and would introduce a circular import: metrics.ts:2 already does `import { DATA_TODAY, WINDOW_DAYS } from './demo/generate'`, so the dependency edge is metrics → generate. Making metrics.ts the home and importing addDays into generate.ts would close that into a cycle. Cleaner fix: extract addDays (and ideally daysBetween) into a tiny shared module like src/lib/date.ts that both import, or simply export it from generate.ts and import into metrics.ts (following the existing direction).
lane: Data layer & domain model (src/lib types, demo generator, RNG, metrics, selectors, formatting/labels/palette, debug surface)
suggestedFix: Export addDays once (metrics.ts is the natural home, or a shared date util) and import it into generate.ts, deleting the duplicate.

title: deltaPct fabricates +100% when prev===0 (but title's "sign/denominator divergence" framing is wrong)
evidence: metrics.ts:87 `const deltaPct = prev !== 0 ? delta / Math.abs(prev) : current !== 0 ? 1 : 0` — any nonzero growth from a zero baseline yields exactly 1. types.ts:240 documents deltaPct as a plain fraction with no "new" state. The +100% then surfaces in two renderers: primitives.tsx:111 `${Math.round(Math.abs(d.deltaPct)*100)}%` → "100%", and lib/ai/report.ts:130-131 via fmtDeltaPct(orders.deltaPct). format.ts:34-39 fmtDeltaPct just does `frac*100` with a sign — it computes NO denominator and preserves the sign correctly.
note: Two separate things. (1) CONFIRMED: the prev===0 fallback fabricates a fixed +100% regardless of magnitude (0→2 orders and 0→500 orders both read +100%), with no "new"/"—" state in KpiDelta or its consumers — a real, if minor, correctness wart. The suggested fix (add an `isNew: boolean` to KpiDelta set when prev===0 && current!==0, and have Delta/report render "new" instead of "100%") is the right call and also helps the live-mile. (2) REFUTED: the title's headline — "sign handling differs between metrics.ts and format.ts and uses inconsistent denominators" — is not supported. Sign handling is consistent (metrics derives sign from the numerator delta; fmtDeltaPct preserves it), and fmtDeltaPct uses no denominator at all, so there is no inconsistency between the two. Math.abs(prev) is correctly the right denominator for negative baselines. Practical impact is small in demo mode since populated multi-day windows rarely have prev===0; it mainly bites today/yesterday single-day ranges on tiny clients/ad sets, so low (arguably nit) is fair.
lane: Data layer & domain model (src/lib types, demo generator, RNG, metrics, selectors, formatting/labels/palette, debug surface)
suggestedFix: For the prev===0 case, surface a distinct 'new' / '—' state in KpiDelta (e.g. a flag) so the UI can render 'new' instead of a misleading +100%, rather than fabricating a percentage.

title: enumerateDates silently truncates at an 800-iteration guard
evidence: src/lib/metrics.ts:121 — `while (cur <= end && guard++ < 800)` does cap the loop at 800 iterations and returns a partial array with no error. enumerateDates has exactly one caller, timeseries() at src/lib/metrics.ts:58. The only custom-range entry path is store.setRangePreset → makeRange (store.ts:105-106, metrics.ts:150-157), and its only UI caller is DateRangeMenu.tsx, where both date inputs are bounded `min={earliestDate()}` (90 days back) and `max={today()}` (DateRangeMenu.tsx:71-72, 80-81). Max reachable span ≈ 90 days; WINDOW_DAYS=90 (demo/generate.ts:30). 90 << 800, so the guard is unreachable in practice.
note: The truncation behavior is real, but the "reachable from user input" claim is overstated. The custom date pickers clamp the span to the 90-day data window via min/max, so the 800 guard can never fire through the real UI — the candidate itself concedes "this never triggers." The only theoretical path is a browser that doesn't hard-enforce input min/max combined with applyCustom only checking start<=end (DateRangeMenu.tsx:27) — but even then the worst outcome is a benign 800-element timeseries of empty-aggregate points (no data exists outside the 90-day window), not a crash or wrong numbers. This is defensive-depth, not a correctness defect. Sharper fix: drop the magic 800 and clamp at the makeRange boundary — e.g. in the 'custom' case, bound start to earliestDate() and end to today() so domain logic, not a UI attribute, is the single source of truth; then enumerateDates needs no guard at all. Severity nit, not low.
lane: Data layer & domain model (src/lib types, demo generator, RNG, metrics, selectors, formatting/labels/palette, debug surface)
suggestedFix: Raise/remove the guard or assert/clamp the range length explicitly, and validate custom ranges (start<=end, bounded span) at the makeRange boundary.

title: poisson(lambda>30) uses a clamped gaussian approximation — standard, not buggy; "undershoot to 0" claim is negligible
evidence: src/lib/rng.ts:78 — `if (lambda > 30) return Math.max(0, Math.round(gaussian(rng, lambda, Math.sqrt(lambda))))`. gaussian is Box-Muller (rng.ts:61-68). Used only at src/lib/demo/generate.ts:492: `poisson(drng, linkClicks * cvr)`, so lambda>30 requires ~30+ daily purchases (a high-volume ad).
note: The candidate is right that this is a normal approximation and right that it's purely cosmetic for a demo, but the specific failure modes it cites are wrong or overstated, so this is partial, not confirmed. (1) "non-integer-adjacent values": false — `Math.round(...)` always returns an integer. (2) "occasionally undershoot to 0 on a low draw": effectively never. Hitting <=0 requires a z-score <= -sqrt(lambda) <= -5.48 sd at lambda=30, i.e. P ~ 2e-8, and rng.ts:78 already wraps it in `Math.max(0, ...)`, so the stated symptom is both astronomically rare AND already clamped — the candidate failed to note the existing clamp. (3) The normal approximation to Poisson for lambda>30 is a textbook, well-accepted technique (good for lambda > ~20), not a defect; the file even self-labels it "crude" (rng.ts:75). The only defensible residual is purely aesthetic: variance/skew shape differs subtly from true Poisson on the rare high-volume day, invisible in the UI (purchases feed revenue/AOV aggregates). Net: real but trivial; nit severity is correct. The suggested fix to clamp to lambda*0.5 would actually be wrong — it would bias the mean upward and truncate legitimate low draws on genuinely high-lambda days; the existing `Math.max(0, ...)` is the right (and sufficient) guard. Recommend no change.
lane: Data layer & domain model (src/lib types, demo generator, RNG, metrics, selectors, formatting/labels/palette, debug surface)
suggestedFix: Acceptable for demo; if tightened, clamp the gaussian fallback to a sensible floor (e.g. lambda*0.5) or use a transformed-rejection Poisson for large lambda.

title: makeCreatives format selection makes 'carousel' rare and slightly skews the documented mix
evidence: generate.ts:111 `const format: CreativeFormat = chance(rng, 0.58) ? 'video' : chance(rng, 0.6) ? 'image' : 'carousel'`. chance(rng,p) is `rng() < p` (rng.ts:56-58), so the nested probabilities are: video 58%, image 0.42*0.6=25.2%, carousel 0.42*0.4=16.8%. CREATIVE_FORMATS = ['video','image','carousel'] (catalog.ts:141) — `grep -rn CREATIVE_FORMATS src/` returns ONLY the declaration line, zero consuming references, so it does not drive selection. By contrast CREATIVE_ANGLES IS consumed via `pick(rng, CREATIVE_ANGLES)` (generate.ts:110), which makes the inconsistency concrete.
note: All factual claims hold: probabilities (~58/25/17), the hardcoded inline selection, and CREATIVE_FORMATS being unused for generation. nit is the right severity — demo-only data, not a correctness bug, and the skew is plausibly intentional. Sharper fix: a weighted table keyed on CREATIVE_FORMATS, e.g. `const FORMAT_WEIGHTS: Record<CreativeFormat, number> = { video: 0.58, image: 0.25, carousel: 0.17 }` plus a small `weightedPick(rng, FORMAT_WEIGHTS)` helper — makes the catalog constant the single source of truth and the mix tunable in one place. Minor caveat: changing the RNG draw pattern (e.g. one `rng()` instead of two `chance()` calls) will shift downstream seeded values, so any golden/snapshot fixtures keyed on the demo seed would need regenerating.
lane: Data layer & domain model (src/lib types, demo generator, RNG, metrics, selectors, formatting/labels/palette, debug surface)
suggestedFix: Drive format selection from a weighted table over CREATIVE_FORMATS (or document the intended split) so the catalog constant is the single source of truth and carousel share is intentional.

title: sample() can underfill chosenCreatives, masked by a dead ?? pick(rng, creatives) duplicate-creative fallback
evidence: rng.ts:47-54: sample() loops `while (out.length < n && copy.length)`, so it returns min(n, arr.length) distinct items — it genuinely caps at arr.length and never duplicates. generate.ts:355: `const nAds = ... intRange(rng, 2, 4)` (max 4, both branches of the ternary are identical 2-4). generate.ts:356: `const chosenCreatives = sample(rng, creatives, nAds)`. generate.ts:106: creative count is 7 (onboarding) or intRange(12,18) otherwise. generate.ts:359: `const creative = chosenCreatives[a] ?? pick(rng, creatives)`. Since nAds<=4 and creatives.length>=7 always, sample always returns exactly nAds distinct entries, so chosenCreatives[a] is never undefined for a in [0,nAds) — the `?? pick(...)` branch is unreachable dead code.
note: Claim is accurate on all counts. The fallback is effectively dead given current parameters (7 creatives is the floor, 4 ads the ceiling, no overlap possible). Two subtleties worth noting: (1) the dead-code masking is the real concern — it reads as if under-filling is handled when it isn't, and if someone later raised nAds above the creative floor (or a future onboarding tier shipped <nAds creatives) the silent fallback would quietly place two ads on the same creativeId within one ad set, which downstream metrics/dedup logic may not expect. (2) pick(rng, creatives) here would also consume an extra rng() draw, perturbing the deterministic stream for everything after it — another reason the fallback firing would be a latent surprise rather than a graceful degrade. Sharper fix than the candidate's: keep an explicit, intentional reuse policy — e.g. `const creative = chosenCreatives[a] ?? chosenCreatives[a % chosenCreatives.length]` if reuse is ever desired (cycles deterministically, no duplicate within the distinct set until exhausted, no extra rng draw), OR a dev-only invariant `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') console.assert(chosenCreatives.length === nAds)`. Severity nit/tech-debt is correct — purely a maintainability/clarity issue in demo-mode data generation, zero current user-visible impact.
lane: Data layer & domain model (src/lib types, demo generator, RNG, metrics, selectors, formatting/labels/palette, debug surface)
suggestedFix: Either assert chosenCreatives.length===nAds (it always should be given counts) or make creative reuse across ads explicit/intentional rather than an implicit ?? fallback.

title: debug.ts runs getDataset() and a console.log at module top-level, but the production-safety risk is already handled at its sole import site
evidence: src/lib/debug.ts:15 `const ds = getDataset()` and src/lib/debug.ts:110 `console.log(...)` both execute at module evaluation, and the file has no internal import.meta.env.DEV guard — all confirmed. BUT the candidate's harm premise ("if it is ever imported in a production bundle") is already prevented: the only importer is src/main.tsx:8-9, `if (import.meta.env.DEV) { void import('./lib/debug') }` — a DEV-gated *dynamic* import. Under Vite, import.meta.env.DEV is statically replaced with false in `vite build`, so the branch is dead-code-eliminated and the chunk is never loaded in production. Also note getDataset() is memoized (src/lib/demo/dataset.ts:3-8: `let _dataset` reused), so the top-level call is not a redundant generation — it shares the app's single instance.
note: File-local facts are correct, but the only consequence that would make this matter (eager generation + console probes shipping to prod) cannot occur with the current code — main.tsx already dev-gates the lone import with a static import.meta.env.DEV check around a dynamic import(), which Vite strips in production. So the suggested fix's second half ("ensure the only import of debug.ts is itself dev-gated") is already satisfied. Severity is nit, not low: there's no live perf or bundle cost. The only residual value of an in-file `if (import.meta.env.DEV)` guard is defense-in-depth against a *future* careless static import elsewhere — reasonable hygiene, but speculative and not a current defect. The candidate is honest that the import site is "outside this lane," which is exactly why it stops short of confirming the real impact: checking that site refutes the harm.
lane: Data layer & domain model (src/lib types, demo generator, RNG, metrics, selectors, formatting/labels/palette, debug surface)
suggestedFix: Guard the whole side-effecting body behind if (import.meta.env.DEV) and ensure the only import of debug.ts is itself dev-gated, so the diagnostics surface and eager generation never reach production.

title: addToCart/LPV funnel ordering is undocumented but not actually inverted
evidence: generate.ts:495 `addToCart = Math.round(purchases * range(drng, 2.6, 4.4) + linkClicks * 0.05)` and generate.ts:496 `landingPageViews = Math.round(linkClicks * range(drng, 0.72, 0.9))` — both confirmed verbatim. purchases ~ poisson(linkClicks*cvr), cvr clamped 0.003–0.09 (line 484, 492). types.ts:188-191 document both fields as "for funnel diagnosis" only. No component in src/components or src/app consumes these for funnel/ordering (grep returned nothing); metrics.ts:29-30 only sums them. No invariant/assert exists in generate.ts.
note: The candidate's own title implies a possible inversion ("addToCart includes a linkClicks term that can exceed purchases-derived intent"), but working the math shows the funnel does NOT invert: addToCart's max is ~linkClicks*(0.09*4.4 + 0.05) ≈ 0.45*linkClicks, while landingPageViews is ~0.72–0.90*linkClicks, so addToCart < landingPageViews in essentially all cases, and both are < linkClicks < impressions. suggestedFix: Add currency_offset to the account fields fetch and to AdAccount; thread it onto the snapshot account record; in applyAction prefer the account's live currency_offset over the static map (keep the map only as a fallback).

title: checkConnection uses edge-shaped graphGet on a node path, parses no data, and reports false success
evidence: graphGet (src/lib/provider/liveProvider.ts:106-130) is hard-wired for edges: it returns T[] (line 106), casts every response to GraphPage<T> = {data: T[], paging?} (lines 96-99, 120), and accumulates via out.push(...(page.data ?? [])) (line 121). checkConnection (line 146) calls it with path `${first.adAccountId}` i.e. a node /act_<id>, not an edge. lane: Provider seam (demo vs live Meta Marketing API)
suggestedFix: Add a node-GET variant of graphGet (no pagination, returns the object) for single-node fetches, and use it in both checkConnection and the account-node fetch; assert the parsed object is non-null.

title: Live writes assume 2xx == success and Undo never issues a compensating Graph POST
evidence: liveProvider.ts:238-240 — POST then `if (!res.ok) return {ok:false}`; `return {ok:true}` for any 2xx with NO `await res.json()` / no `success:true` check (contrast graphGet:116-119 which at least reads body on error, but also only checks res.ok). store.ts:134 captures `restore = captureRestore(...)`; the Undo closure store.ts:148-156 calls `restore()` only — and captureRestore (store.ts:221-226) mutates the in-memory entity directly (`x.status = prevStatus`, `x.dailyBudget = prevBudget`) with zero provider/fetch call, so live Undo never POSTs an inverse to Meta. title: isoDaysAgo computes the insights window in UTC, ignoring the ad account's timezone
evidence: liveProvider.ts:268-272 — isoDaysAgo uses d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate()-n) + d.toISOString().slice(0,10), i.e. pure UTC date math. Lines 163-164 build since=isoDaysAgo(cfg.windowDays), until=isoDaysAgo(0); line 187 passes them as time_range:{since,until} with time_increment:'1' (daily rows). The provider fetches timezone_name at lines 168-170 and stores it on the account (line 178) but never uses it to derive the window. Research docs/research/meta-marketing-api.md:772 (gotcha 5): "date_preset/time_range are in the account's timezone, not UTC ... or daily totals will shift vs Ads Manager"; also line 444 ("YYYY-MM-DD, until inclusive, account TZ"). The claim's UTC-vs-account-TZ mismatch is real.

(1) It is already a known, documented finding: docs/audit/02-meta-integration.md:95-99 logs it as B9 [LOW] with the identical recommendation (build time_range in timezone_name, not UTC) — so it is "known" but NOT "handled" in code; the bug is still live in the source. The practical impact when live is also smaller than "daily totals shift" implies: for a multi-day rollup the only error is at the two window edges (a few hours of spend at the boundary); it's the single-day today/yesterday views that diverge materially from Ads Manager. Sharper fix: since Meta interprets the YYYY-MM-DD since/until in account TZ already, the cleaner correction is to compute "today" in the account's timezone (e.g. via Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone: acct.timezone_name) per-account inside the loop, rather than once in UTC before the loop — note since/until currently live outside the per-account loop (lines 163-164), so a per-account TZ fix also requires moving that computation inside the loop at line 166.

suggestedFix: Derive since/until in each account's timezone (the fetched timezone_name) rather than UTC, or document that the window is approximate and reconcile per account.

title: DOA rule adds a purchases≤1 clause the playbook Trigger C does not have
evidence: engine.ts:71 — `if (hasImprSignal && hasSpendSignal && m7.ctr < T.doaCtrPct && m7.purchases <= 1)`. The playbook Trigger C (adops-kpis-playbook.md:216-222) lists exactly three clauses — `impressions >= 2000`, `ctr_link < 0.5%`, `spend >= MIN_SPEND_JUDGE` — and explicitly annotates "PAUSE (creative DOA; don't wait for purchases)". §4.3:233 reiterates Trigger C is a sanctioned early kill on broken CTR/hook regardless of purchase count. suggestedFix: Drop the m7.purchases≤1 clause to match Trigger C, or lower it to ===0 and document the deviation; rely on the CTR floor + spend gate as the playbook intends.

[]).map(a => a.id)`). sortSuggestions runs only AFTER dedup (engine.ts:365), so it cannot rescue the already-dropped sibling's metrics. title: REALLOCATE spread is computed on raw min/max CPA — one thin outlier ad set can trip it
evidence: engine.ts:234 filters ad sets at `x.m.purchases >= T.minPurchasesToJudge && x.m.spend > 0`, where minPurchasesToJudge=3 (thresholds.ts:12). engine.ts:236-241 sorts cpas, takes best=cpas[0] and worst=cpas[last], computes spread=(worst-best)/best, and fires when spread >= reallocateCpaSpread=0.35 (thresholds.ts:46). cpa is a raw per-set ratio spend/purchases (metrics.ts:38), so worst/best is a true two-point extremum. The confident bar confidentPurchases=30 (thresholds.ts:15) is far above the 3-order judgeable gate used here. The doc's own §4.3 (adops-kpis-playbook.md:232-233) warns variance at low purchase counts is "enormous" and that judging on 1–2 purchases is "the cardinal sin." Two caveats: (1) This is advisory demo-mode output — the suggestion's action is kind:'consolidate'/label 'Open reallocation', i.e. human-reviewed, not auto-executed, so blast radius is a noisy card, not account damage. The scored.length<3 gate (engine.ts:235) requires 3+ qualifying sets but still computes spread on only the two extremes, so the outlier path is live. suggestedFix: Compute spread on a more robust statistic (e.g., median or trimmed best/worst, or require both ends to clear a higher order count), or raise the per-set order threshold for reallocation toward confidentPurchases.

Worth noting WHY the author reached for location.reload(): the store sets `provider` once at creation (store.ts:73) and has NO action to swap it in-place — it even imports persistMode (store.ts:5) but never calls it. So the cleanest fix isn't just 'call init/loadSnapshot' — it requires adding a store action that does persistMode(mode) + new provider + re-run init() to swap providers without a page reload, then optionally clearing only the now-stale snapshot-derived state (applied/dismissed reference suggestion IDs from the old snapshot) while preserving scope/range. Given the low stakes, the lighter-weight fix the candidate offers as an alternative — a one-line confirm() warning that switching modes resets the session — is the pragmatic call. Minor overstatement: 'unsaved exploration' is vague; concretely the only user-meaningful losses are the applied-action activity log and the dismissed set.
suggestedFix: Re-initialize the provider and reload the snapshot via the store (set new provider, call init/loadSnapshot) instead of location.reload(), preserving scope/range/applied state; or warn the user that switching modes resets the session.

title: CreativeLab in-screen avatar switcher silently caps at 6 clients with no overflow affordance (clients 7+ dropped from the row under portfolio scope)
evidence: src/screens/CreativeLab.tsx:82 gates the switcher on scopeClients.length > 1; line 84 renders scopeClients.slice(0, 6) as avatar buttons with no '+N'/dropdown/count fallback. src/lib/selectors.ts:41 — portfolio scope returns ds.clients (ALL clients). src/lib/demo/catalog.ts defines exactly 7 clients (monogram count = 7: Lumière, Forge, Hearthwell, Vela, Nomad, Atlas, Bloom & Branch), so under the default demo portfolio scope the 7th client (Bloom & Branch) is dropped from the avatar row — this is reproducible in shipped demo data, not a hypothetical. HOWEVER: the global ScopeSwitcher (src/components/shell/ScopeSwitcher.tsx:80-103) lists every client uncapped; selecting client 7 there sets scope.kind='client', and CreativeLab.tsx:26 (initial = scope.clientId) resolves the screen to that client, so client 7's Creative Lab data IS reachable — refuting the 'simply unreachable' claim. Also, under portfolio scope the active client defaults to scopeClients[0] (line 26) and can only be reassigned by clicking a visible avatar (index 0-5), so the active client is always within the visible six — refuting 'the active client may not even be in the visible six'. The agency BM holds only 5 clients (catalog.ts bmId lines), so BM scope never overflows; only portfolio scope does.
note: Real but narrower than stated. The genuine defect: the in-screen avatar row silently truncates to 6 with no overflow affordance, so under portfolio scope clients 7+ cannot be selected from within Creative Lab itself. The two scarier framings in the rationale are wrong: (1) clients 7+ are NOT unreachable — the global TopBar ScopeSwitcher reaches any client and CreativeLab honors scope.clientId; (2) the active client can never fall outside the visible six given the index-0 default and click-only reselection. Sharper fix: drop the in-screen avatar switcher's hard slice(0,6) for either a '+N more' popover that reuses the existing ScopeSwitcher list, or simply remove the redundant per-screen switcher entirely and rely on the global ScopeSwitcher (which already scopes the whole app and has no cap) — the per-screen one duplicates that control and is the only thing with the cap bug.
suggestedFix: Add an overflow control (a '+N' dropdown or a searchable client select) so all in-scope clients are reachable, and ensure the currently-selected client is always shown even if it falls outside the first six.

title: Recommendations 'Applied this session' tile is a non-interactive disabled button

suggestedFix: Render the non-interactive stat as a <div> (or a separate presentational variant) rather than a disabled <button>, so it isn't announced as a disabled control.

title: WeeklyReport digest 'up' icon is computed independently of the headline and can disagree with it
evidence: WeeklyReportScreen.tsx:53 sets `up = r.kpis.purchases.delta >= 0 && r.kpis.cpa.delta <= 0`, and lines 66-67 force a binary green TrendingUp / red TrendingDown from it. Also note metrics.ts:93 already provides deltaIsGood() with a null/neutral state for <0.5% moves, used by the Delta component (primitives.tsx:103) for the per-stat deltas on lines 73-75 — so the header icon and the stat deltas on the same card use different logic.

Sharpest fix: drop the bespoke `up` boolean entirely and derive the icon from the headline branch (or its sentiment), reusing the existing deltaIsGood() neutral state so the header icon, headline, and per-stat deltas all agree. A scored composite weighting orders+ROAS is overkill here.
suggestedFix: Either derive the icon from the report's own headline sentiment/direction field if one exists, or relax to a scored composite (e.g. weight orders and ROAS) and consider a neutral state instead of forcing binary up/down.

title: Single ~810 kB JS bundle, no route-level code-splitting
evidence: vite.config.ts:6-17 has no build.rollupOptions/manualChunks — only plugins, resolve.alias, server. src/app/router.tsx:2-9 statically imports all 7 route screens (Overview, Recommendations, Campaigns, CreativeLab, WeeklyReportScreen, ClientsDirectory, SettingsScreen) + AppShell — zero React.lazy/Suspense (grep found none in src/). A fresh `npm run build` emits exactly one chunk: dist/assets/index-DH4qDDYb.js 809.28 kB / gzip 229.73 kB, and Vite prints the verbatim ">500 kB after minification... use dynamic import() / manualChunks" warning. recharts ^2.12.7 + lucide-react ^0.427.0 are app deps (package.json:19,23) bundled up front. LEDGER.md:56-57 self-discloses: "Bundle is a single ~225 KB-gzip chunk — fine for internal use; route-level code-splitting is a known, easy optimization, not done."
note: Fully accurate; not a hidden defect — honestly disclosed in LEDGER and benign for an internal demo (gzip 229 kB transfers fast). Severity low is correct, arguably nit. One sharpening of the fix: lucide-react is tree-shakeable when imported as named icons (it is, via barrel imports), so the dominant heavy dep is recharts. The single highest-leverage move is a manualChunks split pulling recharts (and react/react-dom) into a separate vendor chunk — it's a 4-line vite.config change with zero app-code risk and immediately drops the warning. Combining both (lazy routes + recharts vendor chunk) is ideal but more than "the cheapest" win.
suggestedFix: Lazy-load route screens with React.lazy + Suspense in the router, or set build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks to split recharts/vendor from app code. The router seam already isolates screens, so this is low-risk.

title: currencyOffset still mis-buckets TWD and HUF as zero-decimal (latent live bug)
evidence: liveProvider.ts:259 — `const ZERO_DECIMAL = new Set(['JPY','KRW','VND','CLP','ISK','HUF','TWD','UGX'])`; both HUF and TWD are present, so currencyOffset() (261-265) returns 1 for them. liveProvider.ts:236 — that value is the ONLY multiplier on `daily_budget` writes: `Math.round(req.proposedBudget * currencyOffset(currency))`, so a TWD/HUF budget would POST 100x too small if Meta treats them as two-decimal. liveProvider.ts:170 — loadSnapshot requests only `fields: 'name,currency,timezone_name'`, never `currency_offset`; the AdAccount type (types.ts:53) has no offset field. So the code comment (257-258) "Source from the account in production; this map is the documented fallback" is aspirational — the per-account source does not exist, the static map is the sole path. Gating confirmed: loadSnapshot throws at the structure last-mile (liveProvider.ts:214), so writes can't fire live yet → latent, not active. The repo's own research doc (research/meta-marketing-api.md:768,784) warns "TWD/HUF diverge from raw ISO-4217 — prefer per-account currency_offset," and the audit independently flagged it (02-meta-integration.md:77-81, 07-red-team.md:132, 06-synthesis.md:207).
note: Real and correctly scoped as latent (medium, not high — gated behind the throwing structure-mapping layer and all 7 demo clients are USD, so it never bites today; would mis-scale 100x the moment a non-USD TWD/HUF client is added live). Confidence 8 not 10 on one nuance: the research doc treats TWD/HUF membership as a "⚠️ verify per-account" flag, not a hard-confirmed fact that Meta's currency_offset for them is 100. ISO-4217 does list both as 2-decimal, which supports the bug, but the truly defensible claim is structural rather than about the exact numbers. So prefer the SECOND half of the suggested fix over the first: don't just delete TWD/HUF from the static set (that still leaves a hand-maintained list the docs say can't be trusted for any divergent currency) — add `currency_offset` to the account fields pull (extend liveProvider.ts:170 to `name,currency,currency_offset,timezone_name`), store it on AdAccount, and use the live value with the static map only as a last-resort fallback. That removes the whole class of bug, not just two symptoms.
suggestedFix: Remove 'HUF' and 'TWD' from ZERO_DECIMAL, and prioritize sourcing currency_offset directly from the ad account (GET act_<id>?fields=currency_offset) rather than relying on the static fallback map for budget/bid writes.
